items.title: Hells Four Through Eight: Wailing, Great Wailing, Burning, Intensely Burning, and Uninterrupted

items.zh: 謂彼有情尋求舍宅，便入大鐵室中。彼纔入已，即便火起；由此燒然，若極燒然，遍極燒然。既被燒已，苦痛逼切，發聲號叫。由此因緣，長時受苦，乃至先世所造一切惡不善業未盡未出。故此那落迦名為號叫。又於大號叫大那落迦中，所受苦惱與此差別。謂彼室宅其如胎藏。故此那落迦名大號叫。
items.en: In the Wailing Hell, beings seeking shelter enter a great iron chamber; no sooner have they entered than fire breaks out, burning, intensely burning, entirely and intensely burning, until, overwhelmed by pain, they cry out in anguish. This is why this hell is called Wailing. In the Great Wailing Hell, that very chamber is like a womb — smaller and more confining still. This is why this hell is called Great Wailing.

items.zh: 又於燒熱大那落迦中，多受如是治罰重苦。

謂彼所攝獄卒，以諸有情置無量踰繕那熱、極熱、遍極燒然大鐵𨫼上，左右轉之，表裏燒煿。又如炙魚，以大鐵丳從下貫之，徹頂而出，反覆炙之，令彼有情諸根毛孔及以口中悉皆焰起。復以有情置熱、極熱、遍極燒然大鐵地上，或仰或覆，以熱、極熱、遍極燒然大鐵椎棒，或打或築、遍打遍築，令如肉摶。由此因緣，長時受苦，乃至先世所造一切惡不善業未盡未出。故此那落迦名為燒熱。又於極燒熱大那落迦中，所受苦惱與此差別。謂以三支大熱鐵丳從下貫之，徹其兩膊及頂而出。由此因緣，眼耳鼻口及諸毛孔猛焰流出。又以熱、極熱、遍極燒然大銅鐵鍱遍裹其身。又復倒擲置熱、極熱、遍極燒然彌滿灰水大鐵鑊中而煎煮之。其湯涌沸，令此有情隨湯飄轉，或出或沒，令其血肉及以皮脈悉皆銷爛、唯骨瑣在，尋復漉之，置鐵地上，令其皮肉及以血脈復生如故，還置鑊中。餘如燒熱大那落迦說。由此因緣，長時受苦，乃至先世所造一切惡不善業未盡未出。故此那落迦名極燒熱。
items.en: In the Burning Hell, its guardians place beings upon a vast, burning, intensely burning, entirely and intensely burning iron griddle many yojanas wide, turning them from side to side, roasting them through, inside and out. This is why this hell is called Burning. In the Intensely Burning Hell, three great heated iron spikes are driven up through the body from below, emerging through both shoulders and the crown of the head, so that flame pours out from the eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and every pore. This is why this hell is called Intensely Burning.

items.zh: 又於無間大那落迦中，彼諸有情恒受如是極治罰苦。謂從東方多百踰繕那燒熱、極燒熱、遍極燒然大鐵地上有猛熾火騰焰而來，刺彼有情，穿皮入肉，斷筋破骨，復徹其髓，燒如脂燭，如是舉身皆成猛焰。如從東方，南西北方亦復如是。
items.en: In the Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering, its beings ceaselessly undergo such extreme punishment as this: a fierce, blazing flame comes surging from many hundreds of yojanas to the east, across ground that is burning, intensely burning, entirely and intensely burning, piercing these beings, passing through skin into flesh, severing sinew, shattering bone, and reaching even the marrow, burning them like a wick soaked in oil, until the entire body becomes nothing but raging flame. As from the east, so likewise from the south, west, and north.

items.zh: 由此因緣，彼諸有情與猛焰和雜，唯見火聚從四方來，火焰和雜，無有間隙，所受苦痛亦無間隙，唯聞苦逼號叫之聲，知有眾生。又以鐵箕盛滿燒然、極燒然、遍極燒然猛焰鐵炭而簸剪之。復置熱鐵地上，令登大熱鐵山，上而復下，下而復上。從其口中拔出其舌，以百鐵釘釘而張之，令無皺襵，如張牛皮。復更仰臥熱鐵地上，以熱燒鐵鉗鉗口令開，以燒然、極燒然、遍極燒然大熱鐵丸置其口中，即燒其口及以咽喉，徹於府藏，從下而出。又以洋銅而灌其口，燒喉及口，徹於府[＊]藏，從下流出。所餘苦惱，如極熱說。由此因緣，長時受苦，乃至先世所造一切惡不善業未盡未出。

blocks.text: Today's reading is a single section describing the remaining five hot hells, from Wailing down to Uninterrupted. It is shorter in English than in Chinese because a long passage is untranslated (0296b16–c01): in the Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering beings are mixed with fierce flames, see only masses of fire coming from all four directions with no gap between them, suffer pain without any gap, and know there are other beings only by hearing their cries; they are also made to swallow burning iron and are forced onto blazing iron ground.
With fewer words to read, take time with the commentary's last section, which asks what these descriptions are for.

In the **Wailing Hell** (號叫), beings seek shelter and are driven into a burning iron chamber, where they cry out. The **Great Wailing Hell** (大號叫) is the same, but the chamber "is like a womb". Master Cháng Bǎi: the room is tiny, "like a mother's womb, just a fist across; less space, more oppression". It is a striking image to set beside Day 6 and Day 8: the place of birth reappears here as a place of torment.

In the **Burning Hell** (燒熱), beings are roasted on iron spits and griddles; in the **Intensely Burning Hell** (極燒熱), the heat is more intense still. The treatise piles up details: burning inside and out, flames from every opening. Day 24 told us that beings live half an intermediate eon in the Intensely Burning Hell.

The lowest is the **Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering** (無間, *Avīci*). Master Cháng Bǎi explains five senses of "uninterrupted": in heading to the result (going there directly, without an intermediate state), in suffering, in time, in life (a full intermediate eon), and in form (every part of the body suffering at once). The untranslated passage describes the second: fire and pain with no gap anywhere.

"Those reborn there have, for the most part, committed one of the acts of uninterrupted karma." Master Cháng Bǎi lists the five: killing one's father, killing one's mother, killing an arhat, splitting the saṅgha, and drawing a Buddha's blood. Note "for the most part" again; the treatise does not claim a mechanical one-to-one rule.

It is worth asking directly how a modern reader should take these chapters. Our two teachers never read them as mere metaphors for states of mind; they read them as places beings actually experience. But they also never read them as threats. Three points from the treatise itself shape how they are taught:

items: **Nothing here comes from outside.** The hells form, like everything else, from beings' karma (Day 8). Even Yama is there by his own karma (Day 13), and hell-guardians are themselves "as if transformation-born" from that karma.
**Nothing here is permanent.** However long, these lives end; the seed of good is never destroyed (Day 4), so there is no one beyond change.

**The mind is the place where it starts.** Day 6 showed a being drawn to its rebirth by a false perception it takes for something attractive. The practice implied is to see through appearances now, while one can.

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng often adds a fourth: compassion. Whoever is in such a place was drawn there by delusion, as we could be. These descriptions are meant to make us careful with our own minds and kind towards others.

quiz.q: Both the Wailing and the Great Wailing Hells burn beings in an iron chamber. According to Master Cháng Bǎi, why is the wailing greater in the second?
options: because of the three iron spikes
because the chamber is tiny, like a womb only a fist across — more confined, more oppressive
quiz.why: "That very chamber is like a womb … This is why this hell is called Great Wailing." Master Cháng Bǎi: "The room one enters is tiny, like a mother's womb — just a fist across; less space, more oppression." C belongs to the Intensely Burning Hell, where three spikes pass up through the body and out the shoulders and crown.

quiz.q: According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what five kinds of "uninterrupted" does the Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering involve?
options: uninterrupted in heading to the result, in suffering, in time, in life, and in form
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Uninterrupted means without break — five kinds: in heading to the result, in suffering, in time, in life, and in form." The first means going straight to the result without an intermediate state; throughout an intermediate eon, pain, time, life, and form never break. The text describes flame coming from all four directions, "burning them like a wick soaked in oil."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, who for the most part is reborn in the Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering?
options: those who have committed acts of uninterrupted karma — Master Cháng Bǎi names patricide, matricide, killing an arhat, splitting the saṅgha, and drawing a buddha's blood
quiz.why: "This is why this hell is called Uninterrupted — those reborn there have, for the most part, committed one of the acts of uninterrupted karma." Master Cháng Bǎi lists the five and quotes a sūtra: whoever turns murderous towards parents, teachers, or the virtuous will surely fall there. B is mainly the cause of §30's ghosts. The text adds that this is "only a brief account of the coarser" torments.
